# Interaction & Accessibility Requirements Checklist: Profile

**Purpose**: Validate that entry R4's in-place editing, optimistic-write, loading, messaging and accessibility requirements are complete, unambiguous, consistent and objectively verifiable — before tasks are cut against them
**Created**: 2026-08-30
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Graded against**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md), [research.md](../research.md) and [contracts/](../contracts/).

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are requirements defined for entering edit mode by keyboard, given FR-013 specifies a click and SC-012 requires the whole screen to be completable by keyboard alone? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013, §SC-012]
- [x] CHK002 Is the auto-dismiss interval for a message specified, or left to the implementation? [Gap, Spec §FR-033]
- [x] CHK003 Are stacking requirements for the message host specified — the order messages stack in, and any maximum shown at once? [Gap, Spec §FR-033]
- [x] CHK004 Is the connection-lost banner's own text specified, as distinct from the refusal message that accompanies a blocked write? [Gap, Spec §FR-034]
- [x] CHK005 Is the empty presentation of the five optional fields specified beyond "a quiet placeholder line"? [Clarity, contracts/profile-screen.md *What renders*]
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for the avatar's presentation when it is unset, and when its image fails to load? [Gap, research.md *Assumptions carried forward* 2]
- [x] CHK007 Is the behaviour of a plain Enter inside the multi-line bio specified, given ⌘-enter is defined as the save gesture? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, §FR-009]
- [x] CHK008 Are requirements defined for where focus lands after a save, after a rollback, and after Escape? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, §SC-012]
- [x] CHK009 Are responsive or small-viewport requirements specified for this screen's layout? [Gap]

## Requirement Clarity & Measurability

- [x] CHK010 Can "a skeleton matching the layout it replaces" be objectively evaluated, or does matching rest on reviewer judgement? [Measurability, Spec §FR-031]
- [x] CHK011 Is "data landing MUST NOT shift the layout" expressed as a measurable threshold rather than an absolute nobody can evidence? [Measurability, Spec §FR-031]
- [x] CHK012 Is "grow with its content" bounded — are minimum and maximum rendered heights specified for the bio? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK013 Is "a revisit" defined across client navigation, browser Back, and a full reload — three cases with different cache behaviour? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-032]
- [x] CHK014 Is "each error announced against the field it belongs to" distinguished from "error text associated with the control", or are the two treated as one obligation? [Clarity, Spec §SC-012 vs §FR-035]
- [x] CHK015 Is the order of the nine rendered values fixed by a source a reader of this spec can consult, rather than only by reference to an external section? [Traceability, Spec §FR-006, §FR-024, contracts/profile-screen.md]
- [x] CHK016 Is "the new value appears immediately and before the server has answered" stated in a way a test can observe deterministically? [Measurability, Spec §FR-014, §US1 scenario 6]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK017 Do FR-032's "nothing MUST render from a client cache" and the design's recorded back/forward limitation describe the same behaviour, or does the design narrow the requirement? [Conflict, Spec §FR-032, contracts/ux-conventions.md, research.md D-2]
- [x] CHK018 Are a refused save and a write refused for lost connection specified as one failure path or as two? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014, §FR-034]
- [x] CHK019 Is the in-place editing convention stated identically here and in the entry that owns it, so "exactly as on every other surface" is checkable rather than aspirational? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, `OT-UX-009`]
- [x] CHK020 Do the requirements for shown-not-edited values and for editable values rest on one consistent definition of what makes something a control? [Consistency, Spec §FR-024, §US3]
- [x] CHK021 Is the requirement that no control goes dead on invalid input consistent with the shell entry's disabled-control-with-inline-reason convention this screen declines to use? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017, contracts/ux-conventions.md *What this entry does not land*]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for the interaction between Escape and the blur that Escape may itself cause? [Gap, Spec §FR-013, research.md B-8]
- [x] CHK023 Are requirements specified for two saves whose responses arrive out of order? [Coverage, Gap — Spec §Edge Cases fixes independence, not ordering]
- [x] CHK024 Are requirements defined for an in-progress edit when the screen's own re-query returns a different stored value? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-032, §US5 scenario 3]
- [x] CHK025 Are requirements defined for repeated identical refusals — whether the message host shows one or several? [Gap, Spec §FR-033]
- [x] CHK026 Are requirements defined for a save attempted while offline where the connection returns before the user acts again? [Coverage, Spec §FR-034]
- [x] CHK027 Are requirements defined for the loading state of the change-password link between press and confirmation? [Gap, Spec §FR-026, §FR-029]

## Non-Functional & Accessibility

- [x] CHK028 Are accessibility requirements stated for the two shown-not-edited values, or only for fields and their error text? [Coverage, Spec §FR-035, §FR-024]
- [x] CHK029 Are localization or text-direction requirements specified for this screen, given the application resolves a locale per request? [Gap, Spec §FR-035]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items are numbered sequentially within this file; each domain checklist numbers independently
